source_read: PDF, pp. 1–12 (article number 103909; all pages; text extracted with pdftotext -layout; pp. 3–9 checked on 150-dpi renders; Fig. 1 on a 200-dpi render of p. 4; Table 1 on the rotated p. 6 render; Tables 2–3 on the p. 7 render). Supplementary S1–S2 not read.

claims.overstatement: None material. 'Changed' is justified for the randomized story factors on immediate self-reports, and the claim confines it to what readers said straight after one story. Small wording points: (1) the stories were adapted from a BBC online report about an ecstasy death that occurred in 2019 (p. 3), not necessarily a 2019 report: 'a real BBC report of a 2019 ecstasy death'; (2) the magnitude's 'younger first-time' should be 'younger, had used once or twice' (p. 3; Fig. 1, p. 4), as the statement itself says; (3) 'small to moderate' is fair for d of 0.18 to 0.39 (partial eta squared 0.009 to 0.039, editors' calculation), all below Cohen's 'medium'.
claims.note: Recomputed: d = 0.18 (gender), 0.36 (age), 0.39 (drug) from the printed means and SDs; harm-reduction support older 23.6 against younger 23.0 by group-size-weighted Table 1 cell means (d about 0.12), so the paper's 22.98 against 23.57 is indeed printed in reverse order; ecstasy stories older 23.9 against younger 22.7, heroin stories 23.3 against 23.3; regression n = 868 from F17,850 and F16,851; MANOVA n = 1,238 from the error df; R² steps .068 + .016 + .234 + .251 = .569. One correction for the magnitude: 'within ecstasy stories, F = 4.8, p = .029' is how the paper attaches the statistic, but recomputing from the Table 1 cell means and pooled SD (pooled SD 4.93) gives about 5.4 for the univariate age × drug interaction on support (4.3 to 6.7 allowing for rounding of the cell means) and about 10 for the age difference within the ecstasy stories (8.7 to 11.7); the same method reproduces the printed age main effect (4.6 against 4.5). So F = 4.8 is most likely the interaction test, and the ecstasy-only age difference itself is probably larger than p = .029 suggests (editors' calculation; it does not change the claim's direction or the 'ecstasy only' statement). Also: the Discussion (p. 9) says the age difference in support was in the heroin stories, contradicting the Results and Table 1; the claim correctly follows the Results. The Procedure (p. 5) puts the remaining questionnaires after the story, but the Limitations (p. 9) say empathy and just-world beliefs were measured before it, which bears on the exploratory regression (priming, or the story changing those measures).

anchors.extracted: 1,280 UK adults recruited from the Prolific panel in June 2022; 32 clicked the link but did not proceed, leaving 1,248 (97.5%); eligibility: living in the UK, over 18; sample representative of UK adults on sex, age and ethnicity; a priori power calculation for a medium effect (f = 0.25, power 0.95) gave a minimum of 54.

anchors.locator: Methods › Materials › Stimuli, 1st to 4th paragraphs; Fig. 1 (p. 4)
anchors.extracted: Eight story conditions, participants randomised to one; adapted from a BBC online report of an ecstasy death that occurred in 2019, keeping its branding and length; factors: gender (Jane or John), age with use history (21, used 'once or twice'; 43, regular use for 15 years), drug (ecstasy or heroin); White neutral-expression faces from the Chicago Face Database matched on rated age (21 or 24) and attractiveness; the older template's brother is 48, the young example's 26.

anchors.locator: Methods › Outcomes, 1st paragraph (p. 3, continuing on p. 4) and 2nd paragraph (p. 4)
anchors.extracted: Bespoke nine-item stigma measure towards the depicted person: blame, anger, pity (adapted AQ-9), preventability, responsibility, four social-distance items; 1–9 each, total 9–81, higher = more stigma, alpha .81. Harm-reduction support: six items 1–5 (general programmes, government funding, drug checking, drug consumption rooms, take-home naloxone, opioid agonist therapy), totalled (range 6–30 implied), alpha .88.

Demographics, then randomisation to a story, attention checks on the story's gender, age and drug (no one withdrawn), then the primary outcome, then the remaining questions; under-5-minute completion rule excluded no one.

MANOVA main effects: gender Wilks' Λ = .99, F(2,1229) = 9.1; age Λ = .93, F = 45.2; drug Λ = .94, F = 36.9 (all p < .001); gender × age F = .1, p = .869; gender × drug F = 2.3, p = .099; age × drug Λ = .99, F = 4.9, p = .007. Error df imply 1,238 analysed.

Stigma: male 45.6 (SD 12.1) against female 43.4 (12.6), F(1,1230) = 11.1; older 46.7 (11.8) against younger 42.3 (12.7), F = 40.5; heroin 46.9 (11.5) against ecstasy 42.1 (12.8), F = 50.1; all p < .001. Editors' d 0.18, 0.36, 0.39.

Harm-reduction support higher after older than younger decedents, F(1,1230) = 4.5, p = .035 (printed 22.98 ± 5.09 against 23.57 ± 4.78, younger first by Table 1); no effect of gender (F = .0, p = .802) or drug (F = .0, p = .922); age × drug profile: support higher after the older than the younger ecstasy decedent, F(1,1230) = 4.8, p = .029 (printed 22.7 against 23.89, younger first); three-way interaction F = .1, p = .926.

Condition stigma means 38.6 (Jane, young, ecstasy) to 50.1 (John, old, heroin), F(7,1232) = 14.67, p < .001; support 22.4 to 24.0. Whole sample: age 45.7 ± 15.4, 51.0% women, 57.4% degree, 62.6% left-wing preference. Editors' weighted means: support older 23.6 against younger 23.0; ecstasy stories older 23.9 against younger 22.7; heroin stories 23.3 against 23.3.

Exploratory stigma regression, final R² = .569, F(17,850) = 65.9 (868 participants implied); story factors alone R² = .068; at step 4 belief in a just world B = .222 (b = .111, p < .001), empathic perspective-taking B = −.227 (b = −.118, p < .001), general stigma towards people with substance use problems B = 1.347 (b = .404, p < .001), support for harm reduction B = −.717 (b = −.285), seeing media coverage of a family affected by a drug-related death B = −1.518 (b = −.049, p < .05); familiarity, knowledge and political variables not significant at step 4.

Degree holders 57% against 42% in the UK, left-wing preference 63% against 39% at the 2019 election (balanced across groups); protocol not pre-registered, findings exploratory; empathy and just-world measures presented before the stimuli (possible priming); face-database photographs; single written story may not reflect news consumption; ethnicity not varied.

Authors suggest the older-age effect on support may reflect the longer use history attached to the older decedent; state the age × drug interaction was evident only for the ecstasy death, but in the same paragraph also say support was greater after older than younger heroin deaths (contradicted by Results and Table 1).

key_findings.correction: Brother's age 26 in Fig. 1 against 48 in the p. 3 template verified on a 200-dpi render.
d and partial eta squared recomputed: 0.18, 0.36, 0.39; 0.009, 0.032, 0.039.

Reports the paper faithfully, including the reversed means (weighted Table 1 means recomputed: 23.6 against 23.0; 23.9 against 22.7; heroin 23.3 against 23.3). Add a caution: the F(1,1230) = 4.8 attached to the ecstasy comparison is most likely the univariate age × drug interaction (recomputed about 5.4) rather than the within-ecstasy contrast (about 10); see missed.

reporting_issues.note: Discussion, 6th paragraph (p. 9) against Table 3 (B = −.192, SE .344) and Results p. 8.
Recomputed F = 32.46; the stigma model's 65.9 recomputes to 66.0.

Recomputed: overall White 83.0% with 56.5 in condition 2, 86.7% with 86.5; centre and right weighted from the printed cells 14.8% and 22.5% (printed overall 13.3% and 24.2%), but 13.2% and 24.1% if condition 8's two cells are swapped; cannabis 59.7% > any drug 52.3% in condition 3.

risk_of_bias.note: Some concerns overall (outcome measurement and selection of the reported result). The sex-balance chi-square recomputes to 11.6, df 7, p 0.12.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is defensible: the abstract reports associations with p-values; the gap lies in 'nationally representative', the Discussion's two contradictions and the framing advice from one immediate exposure. Moderate would also be defensible given the number of Discussion errors.

missed: The F(1,1230) = 4.8, p = .029 printed with the older-versus-younger ecstasy comparison (p. 5) is most likely the univariate age × drug interaction on harm-reduction support: from the Table 1 cell means and pooled SD (4.93), the interaction gives F about 5.4 (4.3 to 6.7 allowing for rounding) and the within-ecstasy age contrast about 10 (8.7 to 11.7); the same method reproduces the printed age main effect (4.6 against 4.5). Editors' calculation; cite F = 4.8 as the interaction test, not as the ecstasy simple effect.

can_establish and cannot_establish call the younger decedent 'first-time'; the stimulus says the 21-year-old had used the drug 'once or twice' (p. 3; Fig. 1, p. 4). The same slip is in the claim's magnitude.
